title: Heat & Temperature
source: Science G3 B2 Study sheet pp.40-45; Worksheet Q1-Q3

scenes.t: We measure temperature with a thermometer. The unit is degrees Celsius, written °C.
Water boils at 100 °C and freezes at 0 °C.
Put a warm object next to a cold one, and heat moves from the hot one to the cold one until they are the same temperature.
Heat can move by contact, when things touch: holding a cup of hot coffee, an iron on cloth, or food in a cooking pot.
Heat can also move from a distance, without touching. You feel a heater on a cold night and the Sun on a hot day, even though the Sun is millions of kilometers away!
Some materials let heat move through them easily. They are called heat conductors, like metals. That is why saucepans are made of metal.
Some materials slow heat down. They are called heat insulators, like wool, wood and plastic. Wool coats, scarves and gloves keep us warm.
A pan has a metal body to cook and a plastic or wooden handle so we don't burn our hands. Houses use insulation to keep heat out in summer and in during winter.

items.a: Holding a hot cup; iron on cloth.
Feeling the Sun or a heater without touching.
Slows heat down. Wool, wood, plastic.

activities.title: Conductor or Insulator?
activities.prompt: Does heat pass through it easily?

why.i: It slows the movement of heat.

activities.title: Contact or Distance?
items: feeling a heater across the room

activities.title: Spoon Race
activities.goal: Find out which spoon lets heat travel fastest.
need: a mug of hot tap water (not boiling)
activities.safe: Ask an adult for the hot water. Use hot tap water, never boiling water.

predict.q: On which spoon will the butter melt first?

steps.t: Stick a small piece of butter near the top of each spoon handle.
Ask an adult to stand all three spoons in the mug of hot water at the same time.
Watch carefully. Which butter starts to melt and slide first?
Write the order: first, second, last.

activities.result: The butter on the metal spoon melts first. The wooden and plastic spoons stay cool for much longer.
activities.why: Metal is a heat conductor, so heat travels through it fast. Wood and plastic are insulators.
